title: Dabakan (lashed goblet drum)
summary: The dabakan is a tall single-headed drum of the southern Philippines, carved from wood, bound with rattan and played beside a row of small gongs. Struck with the hands or slim sticks, it gives a deep boom at the middle of the head and a dry slap at the edge, and keeps the gong melody on its steady feet.
howToPlay: The drum stands upright on a woven mat, the head at the top and the body narrowing to the foot.
Open is the centre of the head, Slap the ring round it, Rim the hoop at the top edge and Knock the carved body below the head.
A ring closes on the place to strike. Strike as it lands.
Begin with the open strokes on the beat, then add the slap.
rules: A stroke on the beat is perfect, a near one is good, and extra strokes cost points.
The patterns count four beats to the bar.
heritageNote: In the gong ensembles of the southern Philippines the dabakan keeps time while the gongs play the melody. A good player changes the pattern from one tune to the next, so the drum tells the dancers and the gong players where each tune is going.
credits: Tradition: the Dabakan; patterns written for this game
